When an evicted prefix is reloaded from the host KV tier, the transfer runs the per-token kernel (`transfer_kv_per_layer_mla`) at ~4.3 GB/s no matter how the bytes are laid out, because it pays a per-token indexing cost for every token. title: [Feature] Add rolling-hash repetition detection algorithm
body:
Adds an opt-in `algorithm="rolling_hash"` option to `RepetitionDetectionParams` (added in #35451). The default stays `"naive"` so nothing changes for existing users.

The naive scan has two practical issues:

1. Patterns longer than `max_pattern_size` go undetected, so the paragraph- or JSON-block-sized loops that motivate this feature in the first place often slip through unless the cap is cranked up.
2. Cranking the cap up costs O(L²·K) per step.

The rolling-hash detector uses a double polynomial hash (Mersenne 2^61-1 + 2^31-1, collision probability < 2^-90) with a two-stage filter — a single-token prune on the candidate period L (Stage 1) followed by O(K) range-hash equality on the few survivors (Stage 2). Setting `max_pattern_size=0` removes the upper bound: patterns up to `len(token_ids) // min_count` become reachable.

Replace ngram FULL_MASK Python for-loop with Triton kernel



## Motivation

`NGRAMWorker._prepare_for_speculative_decoding` has an explicit TODO from the original author. ## Purpose

`flashinfer_autotune()` loads a persisted autotune cache into the tuner before the warmup forward. With more than one rank this can deadlock the warmup.

## Motivation

SGLang tokenizes one prompt per request on the `TokenizerManager` event loop, where HuggingFace `tokenizers` runs at ~4-5 MB/s per thread. title: [Perf] Throttle the fully-idle load snapshot publish in on_idle
body:
## Motivation

`Scheduler.on_idle` publishes a load snapshot on every pass while the engine is fully idle. With `--sleep-on-idle` off (the default) the scheduler busy-polls, so each pass walks the queues (`get_loads()`), encodes a `LoadSnapshot`, and writes it to shared memory under an exclusive `flock` — for a payload that cannot change until the next request arrives.

Measured on an idle Qwen2.5-0.5B server (1xH200, default flags): **10 470 publishes/s, 356 ms/s of scheduler CPU** (~0.36 core), each publish costing 0.020 ms (`get_loads`) + 0.011 ms (shm write) — i.e. ~2.1 k `flock` pairs/s and ~10 k shm rewrites/s per idle scheduler.

The stalled no-batch path directly above it already has a wall-clock floor (`LOAD_STALL_REFRESH_S`) for this exact reason ("this path spins without sleeping, so a wall-clock floor bounds the O(queue) get_loads"); the fully-idle path was left unfloored, so …[truncated]

title: [Superseded by #32911] Add HRRN scheduler policy to significantly reduce TTFT
body:
## Motivation

HRRN (Highest Response Ratio Next) is a classic scheduling algorithm — a variant of SJF that is theoretically optimal for mean response time and also mitigates starvation. Prefill is a good fit because per-request work can be approximately estimated by the uncached input length, which makes HRRN feasible.

Two internal runs against real production traffic show that HRRN significantly outperforms the existing `fcfs` / `lpm` / `dfs-weight` policies on avg, p95, and throughput, while slightly reducing p99 (i.e. avoiding starvation).

body:
PEFT adapters trained with `LoraConfig(trainable_token_indices=...)` save compact `token_adapter.trainable_tokens_delta` tensors. The current loader rejects those tensors. This change loads their absolute replacement rows and applies them to each request's input embeddings and selected output logits, including output-head weights omitted by PEFT for tied embeddings.

Users opt in with `--max-lora-trainable-tokens N` / `LLM(max_lora_trainable_tokens=N)`. Storage scales with selected rows and adapter slots. The default of zero allocates no replacement buffers. Ordinary LoRA on other layers can be used together with selected-token rows, and adapter eviction/reload clears the previous rows before slot reuse.
